row.evidence: Holistics' pricing page lists 'Enterprise SSO/SAML' and 'SCIM account provisioning' on the Security Compliance Suite plan ($2000/month for the first 10 users), two tiers above Entry ($800/month).
row.notes: New row. Flat platform pricing: Entry $800, Standard $1000 and Security Compliance Suite $2000 per month on yearly billing (monthly billing $960 / $1200 / $2400), each covering the first 10 users, with additional users at $12.5/month (Entry, Standard) or $15/month (SCS); per-user fields stay null. SCIM shipped in April 2026. The pricing page puts SAML SSO and SCIM on the Security Compliance Suite plan, while the SAML/SSO docs and the SCIM release note say both are on the Custom Plan (see conflicts); either way SCIM is above the team tier. Standard's 'Google SSO' is social sign-in and does not count. SAML SSO must be configured before SCIM. SCIM deprovisioning soft-deletes (user shown as Deleted, data and resource ownership kept, can be restored); roles come only from group-to-role mapping and user attributes cannot be synced. Okta and Entra are configured with the SCIM base URL and token (no catalogue app found). The REST API v2 (users, groups) is available per user via 'Allow API access'; the docs do not tie it to a plan.

plans.name: Security Compliance Suite
plans.price_text: $2000/month (billed yearly; $2400 billed monthly), first 10 users, additional user $15/month

auth.token_source: Settings > Single sign-on > Enable SCIM Provisioning (SCIM API Token, shown once)
auth.notes: Okta sends the token in the Authorization HTTP header; Entra uses it as the Secret Token. Generating a new token invalidates the previous one.

endpoints.notes: Holistics documents user and group sync but not the individual SCIM resource paths.

operations.notes: Profile updates are supported; the docs do not say whether PUT or PATCH is used. Removal deactivates rather than erases.

deprovision.data_retained: User shown as Deleted; data, activity history and resource ownership kept; API key stops working but is kept and works again if the user is restored.

custom.how: User attributes cannot be synced via SCIM; they are managed manually in Holistics.

attributes.notes: Okta mapping documented as email (unique identifier) and displayName; group attributes inferred from group push and membership sync, not listed by name.

roles.how: Group-to-role mapping in Holistics (Viewer < Explorer < Analyst < Admin); default role Viewer; least-privileged role wins when a user is in several mapped groups. Roles cannot be provisioned directly via SCIM.

limitations.text: Provisioning fails when it would exceed the plan's seat limit; existing users with the same email are linked without using extra seats.
Synced users and groups are read-only in Holistics; changes must be made in the IdP.
Existing Admin or Analyst users are downgraded to Viewer if group-to-role mapping is not set up before enabling SCIM.
User attributes cannot be synced via SCIM.

auth.notes: Per-user API key sent in the X-Holistics-Key header; an admin must tick 'Allow API access' for the user. No scopes documented.

capabilities.notes: DELETE /users/{id} is a soft delete (revokes access, keeps resources), so it is recorded as deactivate. Role is set at invite.

endpoints.purpose: Check if email address is used
Add a User to a Group
Remove a User from a Group

audit_log_api.notes: Activity Logs are an in-app dashboard; no audit-log API endpoint found in the API v2 reference.

rate_limits.text: Per user and endpoint: Level 1 120 requests/minute (standard), Level 2 60 (resource-intensive), Level 3 20 (heavy); 429 with Retry-After when exceeded.

okta.notes: okta.com/integrations/holistics/ returns 404. Holistics' Okta guide creates a custom SAML app integration and enables SCIM on it.

entra.notes: learn.microsoft.com holistics-tutorial and holistics-provisioning-tutorial return 404. Holistics documents Entra provisioning with Tenant URL and Secret Token.

citations.title: Auto-provisioning Holistics users with SCIM
citations.quote: Push new users ✓ You assign a new user to the Holistics app in your identity provider Update user profiles ✓ You update a user's name or email in your identity provider Deactivate users ✓ You remove a user from the Holistics app in your identity provider Push groups ✓

citations.title: Set up SCIM with Okta
citations.quote: Under HTTP Header, paste the SCIM API Token from Holistics into the Authorization field.

citations.title: Auto-provisioning Holistics users with SCIM
citations.quote: When you remove or deactivate a user in your identity provider, Holistics deactivates the account instead of erasing it. The user appears as Deleted in the User Management page, but their data and activity history are preserved.

citations.title: Manage users
citations.quote: They can no longer log in, and their API key stops working right away. The key itself is kept rather than revoked, so if you restore the user, their existing API key becomes valid again.

citations.title: Auto-provisioning Holistics users with SCIM
citations.quote: User attributes cannot be synced via SCIM. User attributes must be manually created and managed in Holistics for all users, whether synced or manually created. Roles cannot be provisioned directly via SCIM, only through group-to-role mapping.

citations.title: Auto-provisioning Holistics users with SCIM
citations.quote: If a user belongs to multiple mapped groups, they receive the least privileged role.

citations.title: Auto-provisioning Holistics users with SCIM
citations.quote: When syncing, existing users (same email) get linked without using extra seats, but new users consume seats. Provisioning fails if it exceeds your seat limit.

citations.title: Auto-provisioning Holistics users with SCIM
citations.quote: Synced users are automatically created and managed through your identity provider. They cannot be edited directly in Holistics.

citations.title: Auto-provisioning Holistics users with SCIM
citations.quote: Existing users with Admin or Analyst roles will be downgraded to Viewer if you don't set up group-to-role mapping first.

conflicts.text: The pricing page lists Enterprise SSO/SAML and SCIM account provisioning on the Security Compliance Suite plan ($2000/month), while the SAML/SSO docs say SAML is only on Custom Plans and the April 2026 release note says SCIM is available on the Custom Plan. The row follows the pricing page.

open_questions: SCIM version, base URL pattern, resource endpoints, filtering and pagination are not documented (the base URL is only shown in-app).
Docs do not say whether a SCIM-deactivated (Deleted) user frees a paid seat or whether active sessions are ended.
Pricing page (Security Compliance Suite) and docs/release note (Custom Plan) disagree on which plan carries SAML and SCIM.
The API docs do not say which plans include REST API access.
No Google Workspace, OneLogin or JumpCloud SCIM guidance is published.
